For those I haven’t met yet, I’m Mia, Hannah’s best friend and very proud maid of honor.

When Hannah asked me to give this speech, she said, “Just be yourself.” Then she paused and added, “But remember, my grandparents will be there.” So tonight, you’re getting the family edition of our friendship. It’s a little shorter, but the reviews are excellent.

Being Hannah’s best friend means having someone to celebrate with, someone to call when everything goes wrong, and someone who will tell you honestly that you have something in your teeth—after letting you finish your story.

One of my favorite memories of us is a night when we had very ambitious plans: get dressed up, go somewhere lovely, and have the kind of evening people take pictures of. Instead, we ended up sitting on her kitchen floor, eating takeaway straight from the containers and laughing until we couldn’t remember what had started it.

I couldn’t tell you what we’d planned to celebrate. But I remember feeling completely happy to be there with her.

Hannah has that effect on people. She listens to your whole answer when she asks how you are. She remembers the thing you were worried about and checks in afterward. And if you need her, she shows up—usually with snacks, and occasionally with a plan you weren’t aware you’d agreed to.

So, naturally, when Andrew came along, I had questions.

Was he kind? Could he make her laugh? Did he understand that “I’m almost ready” is an expression of hope, rather than a reliable estimate?

But what won me over was seeing how comfortable Hannah was around him. She could be excited, tired, silly, quiet—whatever the day called for—and he was happy to be beside her.

And Hannah, I noticed the way you talked about him. At first, you tried to sound casual. Very casual. So casual that Andrew somehow featured in every conversation.

“How was your weekend?”

“Good! Andrew thinks—”

“What should we order?”

“Funny you ask, Andrew likes—”

Honestly, Andrew, I felt I knew you quite well before we’d actually met.

Then I got to know you for myself, and I understood. You’re thoughtful, warm, and you make my best friend laugh that wonderful, completely unguarded laugh. You also listen to her stories with enthusiasm, which is particularly impressive now that you’ve heard some of them as many times as I have.

What I love about you together is how much you enjoy each other. You make room for each other’s opinions, you find humor in small things, and you look for each other across a room. Seeing you today, surrounded by everyone who loves you, has been a joy.

Hannah, we’ve shared so many versions of our lives: big dreams, questionable decisions, long conversations, and those ordinary afternoons that somehow become your favorite memories. Standing beside you today is something I will treasure. You’ve been such a generous friend to me, and I’m so happy to see you loved so well.

Andrew, I’m delighted to call you my friend, too. I look forward to many years of dinners, celebrations, and hearing both versions of how you loaded the dishwasher.

My wish for you both is a home full of laughter, patience when it’s needed, and plenty of time to enjoy the life you’re building. May you keep asking each other questions, keep making each other smile, and occasionally abandon your plans for takeaway on the kitchen floor.

Everyone, please raise your glasses.

To Hannah and Andrew—to a beautiful marriage and all the happy, ordinary days ahead. Cheers!"}
